questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook for a dinner party
Popular foods in different countries
How to choose a good restaurant
Good manners and rude behaviour when eating
questions.why: Pippa says they're discussing etiquette: the dos and don'ts of what to do when eating.

questions.q: What eating rule does Pippa remember from growing up?
options: No elbows on the table, though she never knew why
Always finish everything on your plate
Never talk while you are eating a meal
Always wait for the oldest person to start
questions.why: She was always told not to have her elbows on the table, and never really understood why.

questions.q: Why does the student Samuel think etiquette matters?
options: Because his parents are very strict at home
Because it helps you eat faster at lunch
Because first impressions really matter
Because it's part of his college course
questions.why: Samuel says first impressions really matter, as it's about how you present yourself.

questions.q: Which of these does Aya want to see at mealtimes?
options: Eating with your hands, like at home
Eye contact, conversation and cutlery
Complete silence during the whole meal
Everyone using their phones at the table
questions.why: Aya would like to see eye contact, having a conversation and using your cutlery.

questions.q: Why does Aya say her napkin rule might seem 'picky'?
options: She knows others may think it's too strict
She thinks napkins are really unnecessary
Her family never uses napkins at home
She often spills food on her clothes
questions.why: She says 'I know this could be, like, picky for everyone else'.

questions.q: According to Rupert Wesson, why did people start clinking glasses?
options: To make a pleasant sound before drinking
To check that the glasses weren't broken
To start the meal at exactly the same time
Drinks mixed, showing neither was poisoned
questions.why: He says clinking slops drink into each other's cups, showing 'I trust you. You trust me.'

questions.q: What does Rupert say about wearing a hat at the table?
options: It's fine in most countries these days
He wouldn't, and never wears a hat inside
It's only rude at very formal dinners
It's polite if you are the host of the meal
questions.why: He says 'It's not something I would do' and he wouldn't wear a hat inside anyway.

questions.q: What does Pippa conclude about etiquette?
options: The rules are the same in every country
Etiquette is no longer important these days
Rules change, but the aim is to show thanks
Only British people really care about it
questions.why: She says etiquette varies over time and culture, but the point is always to show appreciation.
